G0700.root: probably from [[w:G0142]] (through the idea of exciting emotion)
G0700.strongs: to be agreeable (or by implication, to seek to be so)
senses: In late Gk., esp. in Inscr., to render service to (see M, Th., ICC, 1 Co., ll with; Cremer, 640 f.); [[r:ROM.15.1|Rom 15:1]], 3, [[r:1CO.10.33|1Co 10:33]], [[r:1TH.2.4|1Th 2:4]].† (AS)

(ἀρέσκω), pleasing, agreeable (Hdt., Xen., and later writers; see Cremer, 641 f; MM, see word): with dative of person(s), [[r:JHN.8.29|Jhn 8:29]], [[r:ACT.12.3|Act 12:3]]; before ἐνώπιον, with genitive (Bl., § 37, 1; 40, 7), [[r:1JN.3.22|1Jn 3:22]]; ἀρεστόν ἐστιν, with accusative and inf (El., § 69, 5; 72, 5), [[r:ACT.6.2|Act 6:2.]]† (AS)

Aretas, an Arabian king: [[r:2CO.11.32|2Co 11:32]] (Deiss., BS, 183 f., thinks the proper spelling Ἀρέθας was changed, as Schürer suggests, "by desire to Hellenise a barbaric name by assimilation to ἀρετή").† (AS)

G0703.strongs: properly, manliness (valor), i.e. excellence (intrinsic or attributed)
senses: prop., whatever procures pre-eminent estimation for a person or thing, in Hom. any kind of conspicuous advantage. Later confined by philos. writers to intrinsic eminence-moral goodness, virtue;

of men: [[r:PHP.4.8|Php 4:8]], [[r:2PE.1.5|2Pe 1:5]]; pl. (Isa, Es, ll. with), excellencies: [[r:1PE.2.9|1Pe 2:9]] (the usage appears to be a survival of an early comprehensive sense in which the original idea is blended with the impression which it makes on others, i.e. praise, renown; see Hort, 1 Pe., 129. Deiss., BS, 95 f., thinks it means manifestations of divine power, as in current Gk. speech; cf. also MM, see word)† (AS)
(nom, not in use, exc. in early times: see MM, see word), a lamb: [[r:LUK.10.3|Luk 10:3.]]† (AS)
to number (esp. for payment, MM, see word): [[r:MAT.10.30|Mat 10:30]], [[r:LUK.12.7|Luk 12:7]], [[r:REV.7.9|Rev 7:9]].† (AS)

G0707.strongs: Arimathæa (or Ramah), a place in Palestine

senses: In late Gk., to take a meal, dine: [[r:LUK.11.37|Luk 11:37.]]† (AS)

G0710.root: apparently a comparative of the same as [[w:G0712]]

G0712.root: apparently neuter of a superlative from the same as [[w:G0730]]

senses: (ἀρκέω), sufficient: [[r:MAT.6.34|Mat 6:34]] (on the neut., see B1., § 31, 2); before ἵνα (M, Pr., 210), [[r:MAT.10.25|Mat 10:25]]; with inf., [[r:1PE.4.3|1Pe 4:3]] (for exx., see Deiss., BS, 257; MM, see word).† (AS)

G0714.root: apparently a primary verb (but probably akin to [[w:G0142]] through the idea of raising a barrier)
G0714.strongs: properly, to ward off, i.e. (by implication) to avail (figuratively, be satisfactory)
G0714.kjv: be content, be enough, suffice, be sufficient
senses: to keep off; with dative, to assist.

to suffice: with dative of person(s), Jo 67, [[r:2CO.12.9|2Co 12:9]]; impers., [[r:MAT.25.9|Mat 25:9]], [[r:JHN.14.8|Jhn 14:8]] (MM, see word). Pass., to be satisfied: with dative of thing(s), [[r:LUK.3.14|Luk 3:14]], [[r:1TI.6.8|1Ti 6:8]], [[r:HEB.13.5|Heb 13:5]]; before ἐπί, III Jn 10.† (AS)
ἅρκος (Rec. (cl.) ἅρκιος), -ου, ὁ, ἡ, a bear: [[r:REV.13.2|Rev 13:2.]] (This form is also found in late Inscr.; MM, see word)† (AS)

G0716.root: probably from [[w:G0142]] (perhaps with [[w:G0001]] (as a particle of union) prefixed)
G0716.strongs: a chariot (as raised or fitted together (compare))

senses: Ἁρμαγεδών (WH, Ἃρ Μαγεδών; Rec. Ἀρμαγεδδών, prop. = הַר מְגִדּוֹן), cf. LXX, Μαγεδών, [[r:2CH.35.22|2Ch 35:22]], Μαγεδώ, [[r:JDG.1.27|Jdg 1:27]]; Har-Magedon (AV, Armageddon): [[r:REV.16.16|Rev 16:16]] (see Swete, in l, but also Thayer, see word).† Ἅρ, indecl., [[r:REV.16.16|Rev 16:16]], see, Ἁρμαγεδών Μαγεδών, Magedon: [[r:REV.16.16|Rev 16:16]] (WH, Ἅρ M. for Ἁρμαγεδών, which see).† (AS)

G0718.strongs: to joint, i.e. (figuratively) to woo (reflexively, to betroth)
senses: to join to oneself, marry, take to wife; (b) to give in marriage: [[r:2CO.11.2|2Co 11:2]] (for this there is no direct parallel. But see M, Pr., 160; MM, see word).† (AS)

G0720.root: perhaps from [[w:G0001]] (as a negative particle) and the middle voice of [[w:G4483]]
G0720.strongs: to contradict, i.e. disavow, reject, abnegate
senses: to deny, say no, opposite to είπεῖν: absol., [[r:MAT.26.70|Mat 26:70]], [[r:LUK.8.45|Luk 8:45]]; before ἅτι, [[r:1JN.2.22|1Jn 2:22]]; with inf., [[r:HEB.11.24|Heb 11:24]]

In late Gk. (MM, see word), with accusative of person(s), to deny, refuse to acknowledge, disown: [[r:ACT.3.14|Act 3:14 7:35]]; Ἰησοῦν, [[r:MAT.10.33|Mat 10:33]], [[r:2TI.2.12|2Ti 2:12]], [[r:1JN.2.22|1Jn 2:22]], Ju 4; ἑαυτόν, [[r:LUK.9.23|Luk 9:23]], [[r:2TI.2.13|2Ti 2:13]] (prove false to)
C. accusative of thing(s) (in cl. to refuse), to deny, abjure: [[r:1TI.5.8|1Ti 5:8]], [[r:TIT.2.12|Tit 2:12]], [[r:2TI.3.5|2Ti 3:5]] (cf. ἀπαρνέομαι) (AS)
(dimin. of ἀρήν; see MM, see word), a little lamb, a lamb: [[r:JHN.21.15|Jhn 21:15]], [[r:REV.2.7|Rev 2:7]].† (AS)
(ἄροτρον), later form of ἀρόω, to plough (MM, see word): [[r:LUK.17.7|Luk 17:7]], [[r:1CO.9.10|1Co 9:10]].† (AS)

prop., accusative, to the rule of its formation (Bl., § 27, 2), actively, the act of seizing, robbery (Plut., Deu Puer. Educ., p. 12A), [[r:PHP.2.6|Php 2:6]], AV (Waterland, Works, II, 108; Cremer, 649 f.; Meyer, in l; cf. also JThS, July, 1909, April, 1911; MM, see word).

Passively = ἅρπαγμα ([[r:EZK.22.25|Eze 22:25]], of a lion's prey,), a thing seized, hence, a prize: Phi, l.with, RV (Lft., Ellic., ICC, in l; Donaldson, NCrat., 450 ff.; and esp. Gifford, The Incarnation, 59-71, and reff. in DB, ii, 835 B). The lexical data favour the active meaning, but as they also admit the possibility of the alternative, most modern expositors have accepted the latter as seeming to suit the logic of the passage better. The lexical difficulty, however, remains (MM, see word, esp. the last ref.). As to the usage of St. Paul, he seems inclined to adopt the -μα form where it is appropriate (e.g. [[r:ROM.11.9|Rom 11:9]], where cf. LXX; [[r:1CO.13.9|1Co 13:9]], 2 Co 19), and there is certainly a presumption in favour of the active meaning here from the fact that he does not use the LXX ἅρπαγμα. Suggestions looking to a fresh exegesis are given in JThS, ll with† (AS)

(ἁρπάζω), rapacious: [[r:MAT.7.15|Mat 7:15]], [[r:LUK.18.11|Luk 18:11]]; as subst., a swindler, an extortioner (MM, see word), [[r:1CO.5.10|1Co 5:10-11 6:10]].† (AS)

In MGr. ἀρραβῶνα is an engagement ring; see MM, see word)† (AS)

prince, leader (so in MGr., see Kennedy, Sources, 153): [[r:ACT.3.15|Act 3:15]] (R, txt.) [[r:ACT.5.31|Act 5:31]], [[r:HEB.2.10|Heb 2:10]] (cf. R, mg.) 122 (Cremer, 117).† (AS)

G0765.strongs: irreverent, i.e. (by extension) impious or wicked

G0766.root: from a compound of [[w:G0001]] (as a negative particle) and a presumed σελγής (of uncertain derivation, but apparently meaning continent)
senses: (ἀσελγής, licentious; see MM, see word), licentiousness, wantonness, excess: [[r:MRK.7.22|Mrk 7:22]], [[r:ROM.13.13|Rom 13:13]], [[r:2CO.12.21|2Co 12:21]], [[r:GAL.5.19|Gal 5:19]] (Lft., in l), [[r:EPH.4.19|Eph 4:19]], [[r:1PE.4.3|1Pe 4:3]], [[r:2PE.2.2|2Pe 2:2 2:7 2:18]], Ju 4.† SYN.: ἀσωτία, profligacy, prodigality (see Tr., Syn., § xvi; DB, iii, 46). (AS)

G0767.root: from [[w:G0001]] (as a negative particle) and the base of [[w:G4591]]
senses: (σῆμα, a mark), without mark (in π. of an uncircumcised boy: Deiss., BS, 153; MM, see word). Metaphorical (MM, see word), unknown, obscure: litotes, οὐκ ἄ (Eur., al.), πόλις, [[r:ACT.21.39|Act 21:39.]]† (AS)

G0769.strongs: feebleness (of mind or body); by implication, malady; morally, frailty

G0770.kjv: be diseased, impotent folk (man), (be) sick, (be, be made) weak

G0772.root: from [[w:G0001]] (as a negative particle) and the base of [[w:G4599]]
G0772.strongs: strengthless (in various applications, literal, figurative and moral)
G0772.kjv: more feeble, impotent, sick, without strength, weak(-er, -ness, thing)
senses: ἀσθενής -ές (ἀ- neg., σθένος, strength), without strength, weak, feeble: [[r:1CO.1.27|1Co 1:27 4:10 12:22]], [[r:2CO.10.10|2Co 10:10]], [[r:GAL.4.9|Gal 4:9]], [[r:1TH.5.14|1Th 5:14]], [[r:HEB.7.18|Heb 7:18]], [[r:1PE.3.7|1Pe 3:7]]. Rhetorically, τό ἀ. τ. θεοῦ, God's action of apparent weakness: [[r:1CO.1.25|1Co 1:25]]; of bodily debility, sick, sickly: [[r:MAT.25.39|Mat 25:39]] (Rec.) [[r:MAT.25.43|Mat 25:43-44]], [[r:LUK.9.2|Luk 9:2]] (Rec.) [[r:LUK.10.9|Luk 10:9]], [[r:ACT.4.9|Act 4:9 5:15-16]] In moral and spiritual sense (MM, see word; Cremer, 526), [[r:MAT.26.41|Mat 26:41]], [[r:MRK.14.38|Mrk 14:38]], [[r:ROM.5.6|Rom 5:6]], [[r:1CO.8.7|1Co 8:7 8:9-10 9:22 11:30]].† (AS)

G0773.strongs: Asia, i.e. Asia Minor, or (usually) only its western shore

G0774.strongs: an Asian (i.e. Asiatic) or an inhabitant of Asia
senses: Ἀσιαός, -ή, -όν Asian, of Asia, Asiatic; as subst., ὁ (οἱ) Ἀ.: [[r:ACT.20.4|Act 20:4.]]† (AS)

G0775.strongs: an Asiarch or president of the public festivities in a city of Asia Minor
senses: an Asiarch, one of ten officers elected by the various cities in the province of Asia whose duty it was to celebrate at their own charges the public games and festivals: [[r:ACT.19.31|Act 19:31]] (Strab., Inscr.; DB, see word).† (AS)
(ἄσιτος), fasting, abstinence from food: [[r:ACT.27.21|Act 27:21.]]† SYN.: νηστεία (MM, ut infr.) (AS)
(ἀ- neg., σῖτος) fasting, without eating (cf. MM, see word): [[r:ACT.27.33|Act 27:33.]]† (AS)

G0778.strongs: to elaborate, i.e. (figuratively) train (by implication, strive)

G0779.strongs: a leathern (or skin) bag used as a bottle

G0780.root: adverb from a derivative of the base of [[w:G2237]]

G0782.root: from [[w:G0001]] (as a particle of union) and a presumed form of [[w:G4685]]
G0782.strongs: to enfold in the arms, i.e. (by implication) to salute, (figuratively) to welcome
senses: ἀσπάζομαι depon., to welcome, greet, salute: with accusative of person(s), [[r:MAT.5.47|Mat 5:47]], [[r:MRK.9.15|Mrk 9:15]], [[r:ACT.21.7|Act 21:7]], al.; id. before ἐν φιλήματι, [[r:ROM.16.16|Rom 16:16]], [[r:1CO.16.20|1Co 16:20]], [[r:2CO.13.12|2Co 13:12]], [[r:1TH.5.26|1Th 5:26]], [[r:1PE.5.14|1Pe 5:14]]; τ. ἐκκλησίαν (Deiss., BS, 257), [[r:ACT.18.22|Act 18:22]]; as term. tech. for conveying greetings at the end of a letter (MM, see word), used by an amanuensis (Milligan, NTD, 23), [[r:ROM.16.22|Rom 16:22]] (on the aoristic Pres., here and elsewhere, see M, Pr., 119; Bl., § 56, 4); κατήντησαν... ἀσπασάμενοι (on this constr., see El., § 58, 4; M, Pr., 132, 238), [[r:ACT.25.13|Act 25:13]] (cf. ἀπ-ἀπ-ασπάζομαι).† (AS)

G0783.strongs: a greeting (in person or by letter)
senses: (ἀσπάζομαι), a salutation (so always in RV), greeting: oral, [[r:MAT.23.7|Mat 23:7]], [[r:MRK.12.38|Mrk 12:38]], [[r:LUK.1.29|Luk 1:29, 41 1:44 11:43 20:46]]; written, [[r:1CO.16.21|1Co 16:21]], [[r:COL.4.18|Col 4:18]], [[r:2TH.3.17|2Th 3:17]].† (AS)

ἄ-σπιλος, -ον (ἀ- neg., σπῖλος) spotless, unstained: [[r:1PE.1.19|1Pe 1:19]]; metaphorically, [[r:1TI.6.14|1Ti 6:14]], [[r:JAS.1.27|Jas 1:27]], [[r:2PE.3.14|2Pe 3:14]] (for exx., see MM, see word).† SYN.: ἀμίαντος, ἄμωμος (AS)

G0785.strongs: a buckler (or round shield); used of a serpent (as coiling itself), probably the "asp"

G0786.root: from [[w:G0001]] (as a negative particle) and a derivative of [[w:G4689]]
G0786.strongs: literally, without libation (which usually accompanied a treaty), i.e. (by implication) truceless

G0787.strongs: an assarius or as, a Roman coin
senses: (diminutive of Lat. as), an assarion, a farthing, one-tenth of a drachma: [[r:MAT.10.29|Mat 10:29]], [[r:LUK.12.6|Luk 12:6]] (MM, see word; DB, iii, 428; DCG, ii, 200).† (AS)

G0788.root: neuter comparative of the base of [[w:G1451]]
senses: adv. (compar. of ἄγχι, near), nearer: [[r:ACT.27.13|Act 27:13]] (RV, close in shore; see B1., § 11, 3; 44, 3; poets, Ion, and late prose).† (AS)

G0789.strongs: Assus, a city of Asia MInor
senses: (also Ἀσσός, -οῦ), ή Assos, a city on the E. coast of Asia Minor: [[r:ACT.20.13|Act 20:13-14]] (see: ἆσσον).† (AS)

G0790.root: from [[w:G0001]] (as a negative particle) and a derivative of [[w:G2476]]
senses: (ἄστατος, unstable), to be unsettled, be homeless, lead a vagabond life (Cremer, 738 MM, see word): [[r:1CO.4.11|1Co 4:11]] † (AS)
elegant (in π., of clothing, MM, see word), comely, fair (as in Ex, l.with), [[r:HEB.11.23|Heb 11:23]], [[r:ACT.7.20|Act 7:20]].† (AS)

G0792.strongs: a star (as strown over the sky), literally or figuratively
senses: a star: [[r:MAT.2.2|Mat 2:2, 7-10]]:, [[r:MRK.13.25|Mrk 13:25]], [[r:1CO.15.41|1Co 15:41]], [[r:REV.6.13|Rev 6:13 8:10-12 9:1 12:1, 4]]; metaphorically, ὁ ἀ. ὁ πρωϊνός [[r:REV.2.28|Rev 2:28 22:16]]; ἀ. πλαῆται, Ju 13; ἀ. ἑπτά, symbolizing the angels of the seven churches, [[r:REV.1.16|Rev 1:16, 20 2:1 3:1]] (cf. ἄστρον, and see DCG, ii, 674 f.; MM, see word).† (AS)

G0793.root: from [[w:G0001]] (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of [[w:G4741]]

G0794.root: from [[w:G0001]] (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of στέργω (to cherish affectionately)
senses: (στοργή, family affection, love of kindred, see: ἀγάπη) without natural affection: [[r:ROM.1.31|Rom 1:31]], [[r:2TI.3.3|2Ti 3:3]] (MM, see word).† (AS)

G0795.root: from a compound of [[w:G0001]] (as a negative particle) and στοίχος (an aim)
G0795.strongs: to miss the mark, i.e. (figuratively) deviate from truth
senses: (στόχος, a mark), to miss the mark, fail: with genitive, [[r:1TI.1.6|1Ti 1:6]] (so in π., MM, see word); before περί, [[r:1TI.6.21|1Ti 6:21]], [[r:2TI.2.18|2Ti 2:18]].† (AS)

G0798.strongs: properly, a constellation; put for a single star (natural or artificial)
senses: mostly in pl. (as in cl.), the stars: [[r:LUK.21.25|Luk 21:25]], [[r:ACT.27.20|Act 27:20]], [[r:HEB.11.12|Heb 11:12]];
in sing. (Xen., al.), only of some noted star; the symbol or image of a star, [[r:ACT.7.43|Act 7:43]] (cf. ἀστήρ, and see MM, see word).† (AS)

G0799.root: from [[w:G0001]] (as a negative particle) and a derivative of [[w:G4793]]
